nv12ColorEvidence.report:
# Paired color analysis (CPU only)

The matrix candidate source and binaries were not modified.

## Verified

Bundled FFprobe reports both baseline and NV12 H.264 streams as `yuv420p`, `tv` range and BT.709 primaries/transfer/matrix. Baseline chroma location is **left**; NV12 is **center**. Their decoded PNG ICC profiles are byte-identical (SHA-256 `a1096ca47d80ba9df7f9f8fa87a0b9446d9b6a2c94ab11e4144495616b1eb29b`). A range/metadata/ICC mismatch is therefore not indicated by the encoded files.

Current conversion averages a 2×2 RGB block, producing centered chroma. That is internally consistent with its center attachments, but differs from AVFoundation's baseline left placement and filter. The earlier flat-color test cannot expose this spatial difference.

Using a baseline luminance edge mask (`PIL FIND_EDGES > 20`), audio1080 RGB absolute differences on edges average `[3.75, 2.51, 4.01]`, versus `[1.47, 1.24, 1.72]` away from edges. Visible differences cluster around text, waveform and spectrum. Overall signed channel differences are near zero in this case: `[+0.054,+0.134,-0.015]`, so there is no evidence of a uniform brightness or tint shift.

Flat blue backgrounds differ by a few code values too. The most frequent 4K baseline RGB `(6,18,47)` maps most frequently to candidate `(6,18,44)`. At 1080p, baseline `(7,17,39)` often maps to `(7,16,41)`. These opposite blue signs do not support a simple global matrix/range mistake. One limited-range 8-bit Cb code corresponds to about 2.11 blue code values during BT.709 reconstruction.

## Interpretation and next test

Left versus center sampling and AVFoundation's filter explain spatial edge differences; rounding of intermediate 8-bit Y/Cb/Cr and changed encoder quantization decisions likely contribute to flat-region differences. These latter mechanisms cannot be individually identified from decoded PNGs alone.

The color regression attaches BT.709 metadata to its BGRA reference pixels as well as NV12. Production BGRA pixels have no attachments and rely on AVFoundation's input defaults, so the flat-bar result is a converter range/matrix check rather than strict production parity.

To attempt parity, retain this candidate and create a separate experiment with left metadata plus a centered-on-even-x horizontal chroma reconstruction filter (likely 3-tap horizontal, 2-tap vertical; actual AVFoundation behavior still needs measurement). Test one-pixel RGB/CMY patterns, gray ramps and dark backgrounds with an unattached BGRA reference, comparing raw conversion planes before encoding as well as decoded video. Merely changing the metadata while keeping the same 2×2 box filter would misdescribe the samples.

The 1080p performance gains are within noise and the 4K baseline is bimodal. Keeping this path experimental is preferable to accepting the current image differences for an unconfirmed speed benefit.

receiverSmokeEvidence.report:
# Receiver experiment smoke results

All export cases are 7-second, 420-frame, 60 fps H.264 outputs with a 2-second lead-in and imported audio. Audio scene enables CRT; hybrid scenes enable bloom. These are single correctness smokes, not paired performance trials.

| Case | legacy fps | immediate fps | async fps | async suspensions | suspended seconds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| audio | 240.3 | 237.8 | 240.0 | 410 | 1.460 |
| hybrid | 242.0 | 243.0 | 242.2 | 413 | 1.453 |
| 4k | 70.2 | 43.9 | 44.3 | 412 | 8.862 |

Every decoded frame hash matches exactly across all three modes for every case, checked with bundled FFmpeg framemd5: 420/420 frames per output. Sample PNGs match byte-for-byte. Dimensions, frame rate, ordered PTS and decoded audible onset were checked by the shared runner. MaxFramesInFlight remains 3.

Metal debug layer plus shader validation passed for async hybrid, with no validation errors. Timing from this validation run is excluded.

Cancellation at 0, 0.15 and 0.75 seconds passed for each mode: exactly one completion and removal of partial output. Cancellation during preparation finished around 0.16 seconds overall; during active 4K export completed about 0.19–0.30 seconds after request. Pre-start cancellation preserves an existing destination.

Conclusion: new API alone does not improve the 1080 smokes; both receiver modes are slower in the initial 4K smokes. Root will run paired trials before deciding. The async mode includes scheduling/Task changes and requires state/sendability cleanup for production.
